tools.name: encode_base64
tools.description: Encode UTF-8 text as standard Base64 (padded, A-Z a-z 0-9 + /), for embedding binary-unsafe content in JSON, data URIs, HTTP headers or Basic auth. Returns JSON { encoded }. The output uses the standard alphabet, so it is NOT URL-safe: '+' and '/' must still be percent-escaped before they go in a qu

tools.name: decode_base64
tools.description: Decode a Base64 string back to UTF-8 text. Returns JSON { decoded }. Input is verified by re-encoding, so anything that is not genuine Base64 is rejected with an error instead of returning plausible garbage; binary payloads that are not valid UTF-8 will also fail. tools.name: format_json
tools.description: Validate and re-print a JSON string. tools.name: calculate_percentage
tools.description: Run one of four percentage calculations on two numbers. Returns JSON { operation, result } (plus unit: 'percent' for the 'change' operation). The meaning of value1 and value2 depends on the operation, so read their descriptions before calling. Exact arithmetic, no model involved, no rounding applied

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "decode_jwt" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "calculate_percentage" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.
